goldens.text: BLOCKED: `grep -r foo` is a recursive grep; use the modern tool instead: `rg foo`. rg skips hidden and git-ignored files; add --hidden or -uu when you need them. Defaults: rg for content search, fd for finding files, ast-grep for structural code search, sd for simple replacements, jq/yq for JSON/YAML.

BLOCKED: `find . -name '*.ts' -type f` is a `find` tree search; use the modern tool instead: `fd -e ts -t f`. fd skips hidden and git-ignored files; add -H and/or -I when you need them. Defaults: rg for content search, fd for finding files, ast-grep for structural code search, sd for simple replacements, jq/yq for JSON/YAML.

BLOCKED: `rg` rooted at {home}/code/north-data is an unscoped sweep of the agent-transcript corpus — ~99 GB on disk, 77 GiB of JSONL, growing ~9.5 GiB/day. One such sweep measured 3.5 GB RSS and a quarter of a 24-core machine. Use the index instead:
  convo <terms>            full-text across every provider and account
  convo -x '<literal>'     exact phrase, ids, error strings
  convo session <uuid>     locate one session's transcripts
Same lookups in 0.3-0.4s at ~31 MB, and the index refreshes at query time so it is never stale. Raw search is still allowed once convo names the file: one transcript path, a single day or project directory and deeper, any non-transcript subtree of north-data, `find <root> -maxdepth 2`, `rg --max-depth 2`, or a non-recursive grep. Rare explicit override: `north config agents off corpus-scan-guard` (persistent, live), or a session LAUNCHED with AGENT_NO_AUTHORING_HOOKS=1.

BLOCKED: `rg` rooted at {home}/code/north-data is an unscoped sweep of the agent-transcript corpus — ~99 GB on disk, 77 GiB of JSONL, growing ~9.5 GiB/day. One such sweep measured 3.5 GB RSS and a quarter of a 24-core machine. You also named the same tree twice: ~/.local/state/north is a SYMLINK to ~/code/north-data, so that scans every byte a second time. Use the index instead:
  convo <terms>            full-text across every provider and account
  convo -x '<literal>'     exact phrase, ids, error strings
  convo session <uuid>     locate one session's transcripts
Same lookups in 0.3-0.4s at ~31 MB, and the index refreshes at query time so it is never stale. Raw search is still allowed once convo names the file: one transcript path, a single day or project directory and deeper, any non-transcript subtree of north-data, `find <root> -maxdepth 2`, `rg --max-depth 2`, or a non-recursive grep. Rare explicit override: `north config agents off corpus-scan-guard` (persistent, live), or a session LAUNCHED with AGENT_NO_AUTHORING_HOOKS=1.

BLOCKED: `rg` would perform recursive traversal from a virtual filesystem root at /proc. Do not use recursive content search over /proc, /sys, /dev, or /run. Select one process with `ps -eo pid=,comm=,args=` (or `ps -p PID -o ...`) and query only the needed metadata, for example `readlink -e /proc/PID/cwd`. Use `cat` or `stat` for one known metadata file. If the resolved cwd contains the content of interest, run ordinary scoped `rg` on that filesystem path instead.

BLOCKED: `rg` would perform recursive search rooted at a repository container at {home}/code/proj, traversing main and every worktree. Select one exact checkout or subtree first, then run the scoped search there (for example, `rg --files {home}/code/proj/main`).
